lanes.title: Diesel cost and essential delivery
lanes.question: Are fuel costs becoming actual missed essential deliveries?

sources.title: Food Bank Publications
sources.access_result: Text available through retrieval tool; no raw HTTP material retained
sources.summary: The publication index links an October 2026 newsletter and annual reports. Its displayed page timestamp is October 20, 2026.
limitations: A page timestamp is not the effective date of every linked statement. No dispatch denominator, fuel invoice or missed-delivery cause was established.

sources.title: October 2026 linked newsletter; returned title says July at ACCFB
sources.access_result: 41-line extracted surface; no qualifying weekly dispatch-and-cost packet recovered
sources.summary: Following the October index link returned a 41-line extraction whose title refers to July. A text search found no occurrence of fuel.
limitations: The conflicting month labels were not resolved. Limited extraction may omit image or embedded content. A missing search term is not evidence of no delivery problem, no published records, or no corrective action.

findings.claim: The bounded ACCFB publication check did not recover a matched weekly delivery-and-fuel-cost record; essential-delivery failure and protection remain UNKNOWN.
findings.basis: Inspection limitation, not a finding about the presence or absence of real-world failures.

findings.claim: The earlier EIA price observations and ACCFB procedure/budget statements remain dated context; this recheck adds no operator cost-to-service causal finding.
findings.basis: Reused repository baseline, not a fresh EIA observation.

counterevidence: Retained ACCFB guidance offers donor drop-off and prioritizes partner distributions; it does not say all food-drive pickups stopped.
Staffing, vehicles, route design, demand and other costs remain competing explanations for any future documented constraint.
unknowns: Planned and completed deliveries for a matched week; reasons for misses, actual fuel quantity/expense, and operational reserve.
Whether published alternatives were usable and protected service in the relevant week.
working_buffers: Retained prioritization, donor drop-off and budget adjustment are possible adaptations, with actual capacity and outcomes unverified.
lanes.next_test: Inspect one dated public or voluntarily supplied weekly operator packet joining planned/completed deliveries, reasons for misses, fuel quantities/expense and any used buffer; no contact was made.
lanes.stop_reason: One publication index and its October newsletter link checked within the shared budget; no qualifying record recovered.
lanes.authorship_limits: Recovery specialist reviewed public extraction and retained reports. No site observation, invoices, private data or independent operational audit.

lanes.title: Carrier function and demonstrated electric freight
lanes.question: Which local diesel function can be replaced with demonstrated reliable service?

sources.title: Electrifying Shipping, Navigating the Future with Intelligence
sources.publisher: China Classification Society; interview attributed to Ningbo Ocean Shipping deputy general manager
sources.access_result: Indexed substantive passage available; direct page partially surfaced, later section reads timed out
sources.summary: Indexed interview text reports Ning Yuan Dian Kun began commercial service from Ningbo-Zhoushan to Jiaxing on April 15. It describes a planned paired operation with sister vessel Ning Yuan Dian Peng.
limitations: The direct open returned a page/navigation extract; two later section lookups timed out. The substantive retained passage is indexed text. No voyage logs, delivered cargo denominator, reliability series or measured energy use inspected.
Dian Kun and Dian Peng are different vessels; this is not proof that the previously followed Dian Peng completed regular service.
The publisher and interviewed operator do not constitute independent observations of the same voyage.

findings.claim: A newly inspected July operator interview reports an April commercial launch for Dian Kun; it is historical service-start evidence attributed to the source, not measured dependable service or a local replacement.
findings.basis: Attributed public-source statement; not independent field verification

findings.claim: Regular fulfilled voyages, charging availability, failure recovery, spare capacity and an essential local route that could use this substitution remain UNKNOWN.
findings.basis: The bounded source lacks a matched scheduled/completed-service series; no local transfer feasibility was measured.

counterevidence: A reported commercial start is stronger than a construction plan, but still cannot establish sustained reliability.
Caltrain remains a retained historical passenger-service benchmark; it does not establish available electric freight paths or eliminate continuing diesel freight.
unknowns: Actual duty-cycle performance for the original Dian Peng case; transferable route/terminal compatibility and usable reserve.
Whether any carrier interruption arose from fuel, finance, staffing, equipment, insurance or route-volume constraints.
working_buffers: Charging plus swapping are design-level alternatives in retained electric-vessel records; actual backup capacity is not counted.
Carrier Lifeline preserves consolidation, compatible rail/transload and successor operations as proposals requiring route evidence and willing capacity.
lanes.next_test: Inspect one dated operator or port record for the named vessel that pairs scheduled/completed loaded voyages with charging delays and backup use over a defined period.
lanes.stop_reason: One relevant primary-publisher interview inspected; service-start claim retained with index-access limits and no unverified performance promotion.
lanes.authorship_limits: Public-source review only, with incomplete direct access. No independent voyage measurement or engineering assessment.

lanes.title: Fertilizer pressure and food-service reserve
lanes.question: Do sulfur/phosphate pressures persist across independent producers and farm orders?

sources.title: The Mosaic Company Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
sources.access_result: Text available through retrieval tool; no raw HTTP material retained
sources.summary: Company release reports third-quarter results and a settled fourth-quarter sulfur contract.
limitations: Same disclosure family as the PDF, not a second independent confirmation. Contract terms are not completed future supply.

sources.title: Third Quarter 2026 Results, Exhibit 99.1
sources.access_result: Text available through retrieval tool; no raw HTTP material retained
sources.summary: Mosaic reports phosphate sales of 1.4 million tonnes versus 1.6 million a year earlier, attributing the decline to curtailments involving limited affordable sulfur. It reports a $615/long-ton fourth-quarter sulfur contract.
limitations: Company attribution, not independent proof of every causal driver. Sales are not farm orders fulfilled or nutritional service cover. Prospective contract benefits are unobserved.

sources.title: Nutrien Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
sources.access_result: Text available through retrieval tool; no raw HTTP material retained
sources.summary: Nutrien attributes phosphate earnings pressure to sulfur costs. It reports third-quarter P2O5 output of 342,000 tonnes versus 378,000, while nine-month output was 998,000 versus 993,000.
limitations: Different products/units from Mosaic: quantities are not added. Search and direct displays differ on hour; publication date agrees. Requested -1759 URL redirected to -1761. No matched farm-order fulfillment data.
sources.displayed_time_limit: Search:11:30 a.m.; direct:4:30 p.m.; timezone not established

findings.claim: Two distinct producer disclosures support continuing sulfur-related phosphate pressure through Q3; the farm-order and usable food-reserve parts of the question remain unanswered.
findings.basis: Newly available November 3–4 disclosures concern Q3 observations. Two company lineages support only their attributed operating evidence, not global scarcity or a verified downstream cascade.

findings.claim: No completed replacement sulfur deliveries, exportable donor reserve, unfilled farm-order series or local food-service days are established by this check.
findings.basis: Corporate results and plans do not measure these downstream or reserve quantities.

counterevidence: Nutrien nine-month output was slightly higher; a quarterly fall is not a uniform collapse. Its announced 2027 White Springs closure is attributed to mine economics, not treated as an executed sulfur shutdown.
Production management may preserve cash while reducing output; corporate financial resilience is distinct from customers receiving required nutrients.
unknowns: Distributor/farm order fill rates and agronomic timing; actual alternative sulfur supply after existing commitments.
Current Venezuelan sulfur asset condition and net export availability; local nutrition cover.
working_buffers: Mosaic reports an improved sulfur contract price; realized replenishment remains unverified.
Nutrien reports Aurora reliability improvements and inventory reduction contributing to year-to-date sales; spare donor inventory is not inferred.
lanes.next_test: Inspect one dated distributor or farm-cooperative order-fill record for phosphate fertilizer over a specified application window, including substitutions and delayed or completed orders.
lanes.stop_reason: Two pre-cutoff producer releases inspected; no downstream performance evidence recovered within the bounded cycle.
lanes.authorship_limits: Attributed issuer disclosures only. No independent operational audit, raw-data reconciliation, farm survey or current inventory measurement.
